title: Spending policies: who and what can consume Copilot Credits, and up to how much
summary: The page incorrectly says the policy API accepts delegated permissions only; Microsoft now documents application permissions for policy reads. The policy-creation paths also omit the Identity or Resources choice required inside the wizard.

claims.claim: A spending policy controls which users, groups, agents or environments can consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote:
Control which users and groups can access supported services using identity-based policies.
- Set spending limits for supported users, environments, and agents.

claims.claim: A spending policy selects which services can consume credits.
claims.quote: Use the check box to select the agents and services that can consume credits against the billing method tied to this policy.

claims.claim: Policies can impose a monthly spending limit.
claims.quote: Limited monthly budget: When you select a limited monthly budget, you limit the number of credits that this policy can spend each month.

claims.claim: A policy specifies a billing method.
claims.quote: Select a billing method

claims.where: What it is; Cost and licensing; Governance controls: Interaction
claims.claim: Spending policies are limit-based controls, not purchases or reservations or allocations of credits.
claims.quote: Spending policies are limit-based controls and don't reserve or allocate Copilot Credits to users or groups.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity-based policies follow the person using selected agents and services, such as a group using Cowork.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want a policy to apply to the people who use selected agents and services. For example, a group using Cowork.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Identity-based policy scope can be all users or specific groups.
claims.quote: By default, All users is selected. To target this rule to a subset of users, switch to Specific groups and select the directory group.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; How it works
claims.claim: Identity-based policies support an optional per-user monthly limit.
claims.quote: Select monthly budget limits for users (optional). Use the toggle to select this option and to set a monthly limit for users

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource-based policies follow the agent or environment rather than the identity of the person using it.
claims.quote: Use this option when you want usage to follow an agent or environment rather than the identity of the person using it.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: Resource-based policies can cover specific agents, specific environments or all environments.
claims.quote:
Specific resources: Choose Specific resources when particular agents need their own policy or billing method.
Specific environments: Choose Specific environments when you want to move and manage a limited set of environments first.
All environments: All existing environments

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; controls[4]
claims.claim: Resource-based policies support per-agent limits.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy; controls[4]
claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies are documented for Copilot Studio agents and environments.
claims.quote: Manage Copilot Studio spending in the Microsoft 365 admin center by creating policies for environments or individual agents.

claims.where: What it is: Two kinds of policy
claims.claim: An identity-based policy cannot be converted into a resource-based policy.
claims.quote: You can't convert an existing identity-based policy into a resource-based policy.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Default-policy activation starts at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Get Started.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot and then the Cost Management node.
3. To unlock AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing, select Get Started.

claims.claim: A Global administrator or Billing administrator signs in to activate the default policy.
claims.quote:
Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center with one of the following administrator roles:

- Global administrator
- Billing administrator

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a Graph equivalent for initial default-policy activation or equate allUsersSpendingPolicy creation with that activation.
claims.quote: Searched: "activate" "allUsersSpendingPolicy"; Copilot costManagement activate default spending policy. Opened setup, API overview, spendingpolicy-create, spendingPolicy and allUsersSpendingPolicy references; no initial-activation equivalence stated.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: The default setup targets the entire organisation and all users.
claims.quote: The default setup targets your entire organization and all users. Optionally, you can customize the default spending policy to specific groups

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Why it matters
claims.claim: Initial usage-based billing setup activates the default policy and unlocks experiences gated by usage-based billing.
claims.quote: This section covers the initial setup steps to guide administrators through enabling usage-based billing and creating the first spending policy. This process activates AI experiences, like Cowork, that are gated by usage-based billing.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Additional policies have independent limits and do not inherit the tenant-level limit.
claims.quote: Each additional spending policy that you create has its own independent limit and doesn't inherit the tenant-level limit.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: Policies include configurable alert thresholds.
claims.quote:
Configure policy-level alerts:

- Specify the usage threshold for the policy.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Auto-apply
claims.claim: Auto-apply new services is on by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Auto-apply new services toggle is selected for spending policies.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Auto-apply; What to check
claims.claim: Auto-apply automatically adds future supported services and agents; turning it off requires administrators to add them manually.
claims.quote:
When the setting is on, newly supported Microsoft Copilot services and agents are automatically added to the policy.
When the setting is off, future services and agents aren't automatically included.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: For a user in multiple policies for the same service, the highest per-user limit wins.
claims.quote:
If a user is in more than one policy for the same service, the system assigns the user a policy based on the following order:

1. Highest per-user limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A tie in per-user limits is resolved by the largest overall policy limit.
claims.quote: If tied, the largest overall policy limit

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: A remaining tie is resolved by the most recently created policy.
claims.quote: If still tied, the most recently created policy

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: If no per-user limit is set, the policy's overall limit supplies the per-user value for comparison.
claims.quote: If a policy doesn't have a per-user limit set, the system uses its overall policy limit as the per-user value for this comparison.

claims.where: What it is: How it works; Risks and limits: Overlapping policies
claims.claim: The chosen policy applies in full and policies' limits and settings are not combined.
claims.quote: The chosen policy applies in full and settings from other policies aren't combined.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: For covered Copilot Studio usage, Microsoft 365 admin center policies take precedence over Power Platform admin center controls.
claims.quote: If a spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center covers the environment or agent, its controls take precedence over the Power Platform admin center controls for that usage.

claims.where: What it is: How it works
claims.claim: For Copilot Studio, a resource-based policy takes precedence over an identity-based policy.
claims.quote: Within the Microsoft 365 admin center, a policy for the agent or its environment takes precedence over a policy for the person using the agent.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft's setup guidance recommends setting a per-user limit to prevent runaway spending by one person.
claims.quote: Although this selection is optional, review and set this option for your organization to prevent runaway spending of Copilot Credits by one individual user.

claims.claim: The setup offers an unlimited monthly spending option that imposes no policy-level ceiling.
claims.quote: Don't limit monthly spending - Allows the policy to use credits against the organization's billing method without restrictions.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio resource-policy management is opt-in; existing Power Platform configuration remains until covered.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: All environments; controls[4].note
claims.claim: For covered resources, credit management moves to Microsoft 365 and replaces Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.claim: Consumed Copilot Credits are billed to the subscription selected in the policy's billing method.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are billed to the subscription that you select in the billing method.

claims.claim: When credits for the selected subscription run out, usage continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.
claims.quote: When credits run out for that subscription, usage automatically continues on a pay-as-you-go basis.

claims.claim: When both capacity packs and a subscription with P3 are selected, the billing order is capacity packs, P3, then pay-as-you-go.
claims.quote:
billing is applied in the following order to keep spending predictable:

- Prepaid Capacity packs
- Copilot Credit Pre-purchase plan (P3)
- Pay-as-you-go billing

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance controls: Roles
claims.claim: Global administrators and Billing administrators can set or override a policy's billing method.
claims.quote: You must be a Global administrator or Billing administrator to override or set the billing method.

claims.claim: Billing methods can differ by policy for departmental billing.
claims.quote: This feature enables you to do departmental billing and vary billing methods for each group, department, or set of users.

claims.claim: Service licensing requirements vary, and Microsoft lists Cowork as requiring a Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Cowork (Copilot license required)

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: credit rates
claims.claim: The spending-policy pages do not state service credit rates and instead point to the Copilot Credits licensing guide.
claims.quote: Searched: "spending policies" "credit rates". Opened setup, manage-credits, manage-Studio-costs and billing overview; no service rates given. Overview: "For more information about licensing details for Copilot Credits and services, see the Copilot Credits Guide."

claims.claim: The Consumption tab's estimated cost might not match the bill.
claims.quote: Cost: The estimated cost of your AI usage in local currency, including negotiated rates. It includes usage paid for with prepaid credits and with pay-as-you-go, so it might not match your bill.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Interaction
claims.claim: Reaching a limit removes access to agents and services for the rest of the month until reset.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: The monthly usage period resets on the first of the month.
claims.quote: until credits reset on the first of the month

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit; Governance controls: Watching
claims.claim: Users who reach their limit can request more credits.
claims.quote: When users reach their limit within a policy, they can request more credits

claims.where: Risks and limits: Hitting a limit
claims.claim: A user who reaches a policy limit does not fall back to another policy.
claims.quote: The system keeps the user on the assigned policy and doesn't reevaluate the user against other policies.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: A running task can complete after exceeding the per-user limit.
claims.quote: If a running task exceeds the per-user limit, it can complete without interruption.

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: Excess usage from such a task does not count toward the policy limit.
claims.quote: The excess usage doesn't count toward the policy limit

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun; Open questions: excess billing
claims.claim: Microsoft describes excess usage as not billed at Microsoft's sole discretion.
claims.quote: isn't billed (at Microsoft's sole discretion)

claims.where: Risks and limits: A per-user overrun
claims.claim: That excess does not appear as consumed credits in Cost Management dashboards.
claims.quote: doesn't appear as consumed credits in the Cost Management dashboards (Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management)

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; What to check
claims.claim: Selecting All environments applies the resource-based policy across the tenant.
claims.quote: Selecting All environments makes this change for every environment in the tenant.

claims.where: Risks and limits: All environments; Open questions: timing
claims.claim: A newly linked environment can take up to 12 minutes for a resource-based policy to apply.
claims.quote: After you link an environment to a Microsoft 365 spending policy, allow up to 12 minutes for the new policy to apply.

claims.claim: Removing an environment or deleting its resource-based policy automatically restores the applicable Power Platform policy.
claims.quote: If you remove an environment from a spending policy or delete the resource-based spending policy, the applicable Power Platform admin center policy resumes for that environment automatically.

claims.claim: Resource-based policies do not cover AI Builder features or their credits.
claims.quote: Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises against moving resources that use AI Builder to resource-based policies.
claims.quote: Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: Prior consumption carries forward when a user moves groups and is enforced under the new policy.
claims.quote: Credits consumed under the previous spending policy remain part of the user's consumption history and are accounted for when enforcing the spending limit under the new policy.

claims.claim: After a group move, the Consumption tab's user-level view displays only current usage against the current policy.
claims.quote: Only the current usage against the current spending policy is displayed at a user level in the Consumption tab view.

claims.claim: Policies govern the listed usage-based billing services, and Microsoft says it will add more services.
claims.quote: Microsoft will add more agents and services over time and provide notifications and updated content as they become available.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs readers to a separate pay-as-you-go overview for Copilot Chat, SharePoint agents and the Retrieval API.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat, SharePoint Agents, or Microsoft Copilot Retrieval API (Preview), see Microsoft Copilot pay-as-you-go service overview.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The API is beta; controls API notes
claims.claim: The API is beta, subject to change and unsupported in production.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The API is beta
claims.claim: The policy API accepts delegated permissions only.
claims.quote: Application | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.Read.All | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All, CopilotCostManagement.Read.All
claims.fix: Replace 'the policy API accepts delegated permissions only' with 'the policy create and update operations accept delegated permissions only'. The cited create and update references support that narrower statement; policy reads now document application permissions.

claims.claim: The path to create an identity-based policy ends at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy.
claims.quote: Create and name the policy and then choose Identity as the scope. Use this option when you need to manage usage by users or groups for a supported service.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > + Add spending policy > Identity'. This retains the required policy-type choice rather than ending at the shared wizard entrance.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a policy with the listed @odata.type, displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings properties.
claims.quote: Required properties are displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and serviceSettings.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and the rendered call to 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies'. Move 'The request body sets a concrete @odata.type, displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings' into its note.

claims.claim: A new policy created through Graph starts disabled.
claims.quote: A new policy is created disabled.

claims.claim: Creating a spending policy requires Billing Administrator or Global Administrator at runtime.
claims.quote: At runtime, creating a policy also requires the Billing Administrator or Global Administrator directory role.

claims.claim: The Graph create operation supports delegated work-or-school permissions, not application permissions.
claims.quote:
Delegated (work or school account) | CopilotCostManagement-Policy.ReadWrite.All | Not supported.

claims.claim: The policy PATCH shown changes name, limits and billing method, not audience scope, services or alerts.

claims.claim: The setup page grants AI administrator and License administrator policy, limit, alert and billing-method editing permissions.
claims.quote: AI administrator and License administrator roles can edit spending policies, manage limits and alerts, and billing methods.

claims.claim: AI administrator and License administrator cannot create policies.

claims.claim: Alert thresholds are edited in the policy details fly-out reached through Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy.

The spending policy details fly-out opens, where you can modify its settings. This includes:

claims.claim: Alerts notify and do not stop usage.
claims.quote: Configure notify-only threshold alerts and manage their recipients.

claims.claim: The resource-policy creation path ends at Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy.
claims.quote:
Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy.

claims.fix: Set controls[4].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources'. The existing note correctly identifies Resources, but this required wizard choice must also be in the path.

claims.quote: Searched: "resource" "spendingPolicy" "costManagement" API; Copilot resource based spending policies API. Opened Studio costs, API overview, spendingPolicy, allUsersSpendingPolicy and create references; documented derived policy types target users or groups, not resources.

claims.quote:

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} removes a policy.
claims.quote: Delete spendingPolicy | DELETE /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} | Delete a spending policy.

claims.claim: Deleting a policy does not remove, reallocate or reset credits.
claims.quote: Deleting a spending policy doesn't remove, reallocate, or reset Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Users covered by a deleted policy can continue under another applicable group policy.
claims.quote: If another spending policy applies to a user through group membership, the user continues to consume Copilot Credits under the applicable policy.

claims.claim: Reader roles such as AI Reader and Global Reader can review consumption but cannot change configuration.
claims.quote: These roles provide read-only access to consumption information and don't allow administrators to create or change spending policies, limits, alerts, request policies, or billing methods.

claims.claim: An existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role.
claims.quote: an existing Power Platform role does not itself become a Microsoft 365 role

claims.claim: Microsoft's setup page also lists License Administrator as read-only, conflicting with its editing-permission statement.
claims.quote: AI Reader, Global Reader, License Administrator, and other supported reader-based roles can view consumption dashboards and reports.

claims.claim: Alert emails begin at the threshold and repeat daily until the usage month resets or the policy is adjusted.
claims.quote: Alert emails begin when usage reaches the specified threshold and continue daily until the monthly usage period resets or you adjust the spending policy.

claims.claim: The Cost Management Overview tab refreshes every four hours.
claims.quote: The Overview tab refreshes every 4 hours.

claims.claim: The Consumption tab refreshes every two hours.
claims.quote: The Consumption tab refreshes every 2 hours.

claims.claim: Consumption reports by spending policy, user, group, agent and service.
claims.quote:
The Consumption tab provides reporting experiences for copilot credit usage by:

- Spending policy
- User
- Group
- Agent
- Service

claims.claim: Consumption reporting includes limit utilisation.
claims.quote: Limit utilization: Credit usage divided by the current spending limit.

claims.claim: Administrators review submitted requests on the Credit requests page.
claims.quote: To view and approve credit requests from end users, select View requests. The Credit requests page displays all pending and approved requests.
